docs.title: Floowandereeze & Modding
docs.text:
Floowandereeze & Modding is a Windows desktop tool for replacing visual assets and editing card text in Yu-Gi-Oh! Master Duel.

It currently supports:

  • Card artwork, names, and descriptions
  • Card icons from the game's shared sprite atlas
  • Card faces and sleeves
  • Player icons and coins
  • Deck box textures
  • Duel fields
  • Home backgrounds and wallpapers

The app edits files in your Master Duel installation. Game updates can replace those files, and two mods that change the same bundle can overwrite one another. Read Backups and safe modding before making your first replacement.

docs.title: Start here
docs.text:
1. Follow Getting started to install the app, select the correct player-data folder, and download the asset index.
  2. Read Using the editors for the controls shared by most pages.
  3. Open the guide for the asset you want to change.

docs.title: Editor guides
docs.text:
Editor What it changes Notable tools Cards Card artwork, names, and descriptions Search, favorites, individual and mass text editing Card Icons Small card-related graphics in the shared atlas Atlas-region extraction, replacement, and restore Card Faces Card frame/face textures Replace, extract, and restore Sleeves Card sleeve textures Optional solid or fade-in border, favorites Player Icons Player profile icons Replaces all three resolutions, favorites Deck Boxes Deck box size and orientation textures Normal, Left Facing, and Open artwork; automatic resolutions, favorites Coins Duel coin textures Replaces all three resolutions, favorites Duel Fields Supported duel field surface textures Extract and copy bundle Background The shared home/duel background texture Fixed 1920×1080 replacement Wallpapers Home wallpaper foreground/background pair Extract and copy both bundles Configuration Paths, data, backups, appearance, and bundle settings Steam auto-detection and bulk maintenance

If something does not work as expected, see Troubleshooting.

docs.title: Important limitations
docs.text:
• The application is Windows-focused and expects the Steam installation layout.
  • Close Master Duel before replacing or restoring assets.
  • Master Duel updates may restore original game files. Use Reapply All for saved card-text edits; image mods usually need to be replaced again.
  • Field layouts are not standardized, so some fields are unsupported or may replace the wrong portion.
  • Wallpapers may contain extra layers and effects that this app does not change.

docs.title: Regex mass editing
docs.text:
Open Mass Edit on the Cards page. Choose All cards, Selected cards, Search results, or Favorites. All scopes use the current TCG/OCG region. Use Ctrl-click or Shift-click in the card list to select multiple cards before opening the dialog. Search results uses the last executed search currently displayed in the list; it is empty when no search is displayed or the favorites filter is active. Favorites includes every favorite, regardless of the search.

Enter a Python regular expression and replacement text (capture references such as \1 are supported), then choose names, descriptions, or both. Empty replacement text deletes matches. Existing text edits are the starting text.

Click Preview Changes to see the number of affected cards and replacements. Choose an affected card to inspect its full before/after text and line differences. The Differences block highlights removed lines in red and added lines in green, with subtle matching backgrounds. Diff headers are blue and bold; newline notes are muted and italic. Colors adapt to light and dark themes. The - and + prefixes remain visible so changes can also be identified without color.

Identical replacements do not count as changes. Previewing does not write game files. Apply Changes is enabled only after a preview with actual changes; changing any input or scope requires another preview. Applying writes only the chosen cards. Wait for the operation to finish before closing the app.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Windows 10 or later
  • Yu-Gi-Oh! Master Duel installed through Steam
  • The in-game data download completed for the player profile you want to mod

Python is only required when running the project from source.

docs.title: Install and launch
docs.text:
For the packaged application:

  1. Download the latest Windows executable from the project's GitHub Releases.
  2. Put it in a folder where you want the app's database, exports, bundle copies, and backups to remain.
  3. Close Master Duel.
  4. Run the executable.

Windows may show a SmartScreen warning for an unsigned build. Confirm that you downloaded the file from the project's release page before choosing to run it.

docs.title: Select your game data
docs.text:
On a new installation, only Configuration is available until a valid game path is saved.

The easiest option is Auto-detect. It searches your Steam libraries and lets you choose among the detected player profiles.

For manual selection, choose the player-ID folder under:

<Steam library>\steamapps\common\Yu-Gi-Oh!  Master Duel\LocalData\<player ID>

Select the folder whose contents begin with directories such as 0000; do not select LocalData, masterduel_Data, or data.unity3d itself. The placeholder profile folder 00000000 is not a usable player profile.

After saving the path, the app starts its first data update if no local data version exists. Wait for all update tasks to finish, then restart the application to load the editor pages.

docs.title: Enable backups before editing
docs.text:
Backups are disabled by default. On Configuration, enable Backups before your first replacement. The first replacement of an asset then saves its current texture under backups\<asset type>.

A backup only protects the texture captured when it was created. Clearing backups is permanent, and enabling backups after an asset was already changed cannot recreate the original texture.

docs.title: Make a first replacement
docs.text:
1. Open an editor from the top toolbar.
  2. Select an asset from Results.
  3. Choose a PNG or JPEG with Select, or drag an image onto the page.
  4. Compare Current and Preview.
  5. Choose Replace and wait for the success notification.
  6. Start Master Duel and check the asset in the game.

PNG is recommended, especially when transparency matters. The app resizes images as required by each asset, but using the same aspect ratio as the current texture avoids stretching or empty space.

docs.title: Where files are saved
docs.text:
Folders are created beside the application (or in the current working directory when running from source):

Folder Contents images\<asset type> PNG textures created with Extract bundles\<asset type> Original game bundles created with Copy backups\<asset type> Automatic texture backups used by Restore

The Background editor exports its texture directly under images, while most other editors use a type-specific subfolder.

docs.title: Only Configuration is available
docs.text:
The saved game path is missing or invalid. Use Auto-detect, or manually select the player-ID folder under Master Duel's LocalData directory. Restart the app after saving a valid path.

If manual selection reports that the Unity3D file cannot be found, check that the path ends at the player ID and that the in-game data download has completed.

docs.title: Auto-detect finds no profiles
docs.text:
• Confirm that Master Duel was installed with Steam and launched at least once.
  • Complete the game's data download.
  • If Steam or the game is in an unusual location, use Select and browse to the player-ID folder manually.
  • With multiple Steam accounts, verify that you chose the profile containing the assets you use in game.

docs.title: An editor is missing assets or fails to load
docs.text:
Open Configuration and choose Check to download the latest card and asset index. Restart the app afterward. Individual tabs display an error panel if their data could not be loaded; that message is useful when reporting a bug.

Some duel fields are intentionally omitted because their textures do not follow a layout the editor supports.

docs.title: Replace does nothing or is disabled
docs.text:
Select an asset in Results and select or drop a source image. Card Icons explicitly require both before Replace becomes available. Use a PNG or JPEG if a dragged file is not accepted.

Close Master Duel before trying again. The game or another process may be holding a bundle open.

docs.title: A replacement looks stretched, cropped, or transparent
docs.text:
• Start with an image matching the original texture's aspect ratio.
  • Use PNG when alpha transparency is required.
  • Extract the original texture to use its canvas dimensions as a template.
  • For Wallpaper, read its layer limitations.
  • For Fields, the editor's selected region or orientation may not match that particular field.

docs.title: Restore says that no backup was found
docs.text: The asset was changed before backups were enabled, the backup was cleared, or a backup was never created for that asset. The app cannot restore an original that was never backed up. Steam's file verification can restore game files, but it may remove all installed mods.

docs.title: A game update removed my mods
docs.text: This is expected when the update replaces modified bundles. Refresh app data with Check, then replace the image assets again. Use Reapply All to write your saved card-name and description edits back to the current game files.

docs.title: Card text editing fails or takes a long time
docs.text:
Card text edits, regex replacements, restoration and reapplying saved edits can take noticeably longer than image replacement. Wait for the completion message and do not close the app during the operation.

If the app reports that a specific TextAsset cannot be found, run Check first. Do not keep retrying against out-of-date game data.

docs.title: Reporting a problem
docs.text:
Open an issue in the GitHub repository and include:

  • The application version or release filename
  • Your Windows version
  • The editor and action involved
  • The exact notification or error-panel text
  • Whether Master Duel had just updated
  • A screenshot with player IDs and personal paths hidden

docs.title: Using the Editors
docs.text: Most asset pages follow the same workflow: select an asset, choose a source image, inspect the preview, and replace the game texture.

docs.title: Page layout
docs.text:
• Current shows the texture currently installed in the game files.
  • Preview shows the selected source image. It is a visual guide; final resizing and processing happen during replacement.
  • Image source shows the chosen file path. Use Select or drag an image anywhere onto the page.
  • Results contains the available assets. Select one to enable its actions.
  • The horizontal grip between the editor and results can be dragged on the responsive grid pages. Its position is remembered separately for each editor.

The application has a minimum window size of 960×540 and opens maximized. Preview panels and result grids adapt to the available space.

docs.title: Common actions
docs.text:
Action Result Select Chooses a PNG or JPEG source image and updates Preview. Replace Writes the processed image into the selected game asset. Extract Saves the selected texture as a PNG under images. Multi-size or multi-layer assets export every relevant texture. Copy Copies the unedited Unity bundle under bundles. Use this when another modding tool needs the whole bundle. Restore Replaces the selected texture using the app's backup, if one exists. Favorite Marks the selected item for the editor's Favorites filter.

Buttons remain disabled until the required asset or image has been selected. A notification in the application reports success, missing backups, and errors.

docs.title: Image preparation
docs.text:
• Use PNG for artwork with transparency; use PNG or JPEG for opaque artwork.
  • Match the current asset's aspect ratio whenever possible.
  • Keep important content away from the extreme edges, since the game may mask or crop textures.
  • Animated GIFs are not preserved as animations.
  • The app converts and resizes the source for the target texture. Player icons and coins are written to small, medium, and large bundles automatically.

Deck boxes have a Texture variant selector for Normal, Left Facing, and Open artwork; resolutions are handled automatically. See the Deck Box Editor guide.

docs.title: Backups and safe modding
docs.text:
Enable backups on Configuration before replacing anything. For most editors, the app captures the current texture only once, immediately before the first replacement.

Recommended workflow:

  1. Close Master Duel.
  2. Enable backups.
  3. Extract the original texture or copy its bundle if you want an additional manual copy.
  4. Replace one asset and test it in game before making many changes.
  5. Keep your source images outside the game's folders so they survive game updates.

Restore is not a mod conflict manager. If another mod or game update changed the same bundle before the backup was created, the backup may contain that changed version. Clear Backups permanently removes the app's automatic backup images.

docs.title: Game updates and mod conflicts
docs.text:
Master Duel can redownload changed files during an update. Any other mod that replaces the same Unity bundle can also overwrite your changes, or be overwritten by this app.

Shared-file editors deserve extra care:

  • Background, Card Faces, and Card Icons modify textures inside masterduel_Data\data.unity3d.
  • Wallpapers modify both a foreground and a background bundle.
  • Card text updates shared metadata bundles that affect every card.

After a game update, open Configuration, use Check to refresh the app's asset data, and then reapply your mods. Saved card text can be reapplied with Reapply All.

docs.title: Summon animations
docs.text: See the Summon Animation Editor to select a card and replace its summon animation from GIFs, MP4 videos or PNG frames, using the region and game path from Configuration. High quality is selected by default; the checkbox targets lower quality instead.

docs.title: Recreate documentation screenshots
docs.text: tools/capture_docs.py opens the real PySide6 main window, loads assets from the development database and installed game, selects an asset in each editor, and saves PNG captures. It uses the app's widgets, theme, toolbar, search and image preparation code. No mock widgets or invented asset records are used.

docs.title: Prepare and capture
docs.text:
1. Install the runtime dependencies in .venv and configure the app's Game Path. Use Check in Configuration to populate the development database. Download the assets you want to show through Master Duel, then close the game.
  2. From the repository root, rebuild the generated Qt modules and capture:

powershell .\.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1 .\build_qt.ps1 python tools/capture_docs.py --memory-warning

  1. Inspect the updated PNGs in docs/assets/ui/. The helper recreates missing images and replaces existing screenshots there by default. Each saved image's absolute path is printed in the terminal. build/docs-captures/manifest.json records the Qt version, capture dimensions and selected asset names.

To regenerate just the Deck Box screenshot used by the documentation:

python tools/capture_docs.py --pages deck_box

Older versions saved only to build/docs-captures/; those images did not update the documentation until copied into docs/assets/ui/.

The helper maximizes the window to the desktop by default, matching normal app startup. Qt saves the screen's native pixel density; the manifest records each PNG's actual and logical sizes and the window mode. The responsive editor splitters reserve space for at least two complete selector rows, and the helper verifies the visible rows before accepting each capture. The window appears briefly and switches tabs automatically; let the run finish without interacting with it. Initial thumbnail loading can take some time. Captures include the application contents and toolbar, without the operating system's title bar or desktop.

Capture only selected pages, use another database, or choose a different card search:

python tools/capture_docs.py --pages deck_box coin card --card-search "Blue-Eyes"
python tools/capture_docs.py --database local/development.db --output build/review-captures

--pages accepts config, sleeve, card, card_icon, face, background, icon, field, wallpaper, coin, deck_box, summon-animation and backups. For a fixed window size, use --windowed --width 1600 --height 1000 (minimum 1280 × 900). --offscreen also uses the fixed window size and renders without displaying a window; platform styles can differ, so use the default maximized Windows capture for published screenshots.

docs.title: Data and privacy
docs.text:
The helper opens the source SQLite database read-only and uses SQLite's backup API to make a consistent temporary copy under build/. App migrations, configuration callbacks and favorite state changes affect only that copy. Qt settings and image-processing temporary files are isolated too. The helper never presses Replace, Restore, Check, Import or Remove, and never writes game bundles. Backups uses the real repository backup inventory for display only.

Configuration shows a generic example game path, clears the custom background path, and uses the shipped application background. These are display substitutions; the real installation path is still used internally to read textures. Review every image before publication, especially asset names, metadata repository/branch settings, and backup filenames, which reflect your local data.

For static editors the helper saves the selected installed artwork to a temporary examples/ image and loads it through the normal source-image handler. Current and Preview therefore deliberately show the same artwork. This demonstrates the actual prepared UI without applying a mod. Card Icons selects an entry with integer texture dimensions because the current preview handler cannot resize fractional dimensions in legacy sprite metadata. Database contents, installed mods, missing bundles and platform fonts can change the output. A failed page, unexpected modal error or missing preview stops the run instead of publishing a placeholder; earlier PNGs can remain in the review folder.

docs.title: Mass Edit popup
docs.text:
Capturing card also saves mass_edit.png. The helper clicks the Cards page's Mass Edit action, chooses Search results, and previews adding (example) to the selected card's name. The popup shows real scope counts, before/after text and highlighted differences from the development data. It then cancels the dialog without applying the changes. The popup retains its normal dialog size while the main app stays maximized.

python tools/capture_docs.py --pages card

docs.title: Summon previews
docs.text:
The default summon capture saves both summon-animation.png with a real card selected and summon-frames.png with its installed card artwork imported as a one-frame PNG sequence. The latter is a real prepared preview against the installed animation bundles; it does not demonstrate moving source artwork. Selecting a different summon requires matching card artwork in the regional card metadata. You can instead supply your own GIF, MP4 or PNG frames folder:

python tools/capture_docs.py --pages summon-animation --summon-search "Blue-Eyes White Dragon" --summon-source local/example.gif

With a supplied source, this saves only summon-frames.png, pauses playback near the middle, and shows a neutral source filename. Preparation runs through the app's normal worker and validation; no replacement is applied. Use an input small enough to avoid the large-import confirmation: the helper cancels unexpected dialogs and fails the capture.

--memory-warning adds summon-memory-warning.png when using the default extracted artwork. It creates a real 6000 × 6000 PNG example in the temporary folder, starts the normal import, captures the resulting Large animation import dialog, and cancels it. The warning comes from the actual input dimensions and memory estimate; metadata and the warning text are not mocked. Enlarging the example briefly uses additional memory, but the expensive conversion is never approved.

docs.title: Publish reviewed captures
docs.text:
The configuration guides share config.png, and the shared editor layout guide reuses deck_box.png. All generated PNG filenames match the current documentation image references. The default command updates them directly. To review a separate capture set first, use --output; its manifest is saved beside its PNGs. Then copy the reviewed images into the documentation:

python tools/capture_docs.py --memory-warning --output build/review-captures
# Inspect build/review-captures/*.png before copying.
Copy-Item build/review-captures/*.png docs/assets/ui/

After copying the reviewed images, update any captions that describe synthetic data and validate the documentation:

python -m mkdocs build --strict --site-dir build/docs-preview

docs.title: Run from source
docs.text:
Developers can use the repository's PowerShell workflow:

python -m venv .venv
.\.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
pip install -r requirements.txt
.\dev.ps1

dev.ps1 activates .venv, regenerates the Qt UI/resources, and launches main.py. The project currently targets Python 3.11 for development.

docs.title: Background Editor
docs.text: The Background Editor changes the shared 1920×1080 texture used on the home screen and in many menu screens. This is different from the custom application background configured on the Configuration page.

docs.title: Replace the background
docs.text:
1. Choose a PNG or JPEG with Select, or drag it onto the page.
  2. Choose Replace.

The source is resized to exactly 1920×1080 with high-quality resampling. Use a 16:9 source to avoid distortion. The Current preview refreshes after replacement.

docs.title: Extract and restore
docs.text:
• Extract saves the current texture under images.
  • Restore writes the saved automatic backup back to the shared Unity data file.

Enable backups before the first replacement. Background uses one special backup file rather than a type-specific bundle backup.

docs.title: Important limitation
docs.text: The background is stored in masterduel_Data\data.unity3d. Master Duel updates and other mods that replace this file can remove the background change, along with Card Face or Card Icon changes stored in the same file.

docs.title: Backups
docs.text:
The Backups tab uses the backup icon in the navigation toolbar.

The Backups tab lists files saved in the tool's local backups/ directory. It works even before a game path is configured. Open the tab or click Refresh to update the inventory after editing assets.

docs.title: Choose files
docs.text:
The table shows each backup's category, relative file path, and size. Use Category to filter the table, then choose an Action scope:

  • Everything includes all backups, including categories hidden by the filter.
  • Current category includes every backup in the chosen category. Choose a specific category first.
  • Selected backups includes the highlighted rows. Use Ctrl-click or Shift-click to choose multiple files.

Player icons and card icons share the Player & Card Icons category. Cards also includes overframe framing backups, and deck box resolutions are listed separately. Other backup folders appear under their folder names.

docs.title: Export
docs.text: Choose a scope, click Export ZIP…, and select a destination. The archive preserves paths relative to backups/, so it can be imported into another copy of the tool. Exporting leaves the local backups in place.

docs.title: Import
docs.text:
1. Click Import ZIP… and choose an exported archive.
  2. In the archive preview, choose everything, a category, or individual rows.
  3. Click Import. If files already exist, choose Yes to replace them, No to keep them and import only new files, or Cancel to stop.

Archives must store files directly under their category folders, for example cards/12345678.png, rather than inside an extra backups/ folder. Root-level background files and nested overframe files retain their original paths. Unsafe paths, duplicate paths, symbolic links, and archives over 4 GiB or 100,000 files are rejected. Selected files are read and checked before local files are changed; an operating-system write failure can still leave a partially completed import. Refresh the inventory and retry after resolving the failure.

Import stores backup files; use the relevant editor’s Restore control to apply them to the game. Archives do not include saved card text edits, settings, or the game itself. Overframe framing backups work only with the player profile they were created for; importing them does not transfer them to another profile.

docs.title: Remove
docs.text:
Choose a scope and click Remove backups…, then confirm the displayed file count. Removal is permanent, so export any files you may need first. Removing a backup does not restore or otherwise change the game asset. Backup indicators in the editors are updated after imports and removals.

Automatic backup creation is still controlled in Configuration. Backups are not created retroactively.

docs.title: Summon animation originals
docs.text: Summon Animations contains the original animation files and the information needed to restore them. Export or import the complete category, keeping each manifest.json with its adjacent original.bundle. Restore animations from Summons; importing a ZIP does not change game files.

docs.title: Card Icon Editor
docs.text: The Card Icon Editor changes small card-related graphics stored inside Master Duel's shared card sprite atlas.

docs.title: Find an asset
docs.text:
Results show asset names. Hover over a shortened label to see its full name. The selected asset's name also appears above the editor. Assets without a translated name retain their code.

Type at least three characters in the search bar, then press Enter, click Search, or choose a completion suggestion. Search matches part of the name without case sensitivity. Clear the search bar to show all results again.

After updating the app, use Check in Configuration to download the new names, then restart the app. Favorites and backups are preserved.

docs.title: Replace an icon
docs.text:
1. Select an icon from Results.
  2. Choose a PNG or JPEG with Select, or drag an image onto the page.
  3. Compare Current and Preview.
  4. Choose Replace.

The app resizes the source to the selected atlas region and replaces the complete region, including transparent pixels. PNG is strongly recommended when the icon needs transparency.

docs.title: Extract and restore
docs.text:
• Extract crops the selected region from the atlas and saves it under images\icons using the icon's name.
  • Restore patches the backed-up region into the atlas.

Automatic backup captures the selected region immediately before its first replacement, provided backups are enabled.

docs.title: Important limitation
docs.text: All card icons share masterduel_Data\data.unity3d. A game update or another mod that replaces this file may remove every card-icon change, plus other modifications stored in the same file. Refresh the app data after game updates before editing the atlas again.

docs.title: Card Editor
docs.text: The Card Editor replaces card artwork and edits card names and descriptions. It also provides search, favorites, extraction, bundle copying, and regular-expression text replacement.

docs.title: Find and select a card
docs.text:
Enter at least three characters and press Enter or use the search button. Search is case-insensitive and matches partial original card names. The autocomplete list can be used for quick selection.

  • Search Description includes original card descriptions in the search.
  • Search Bundle includes bundle names in the search. Partial bundle names work, and this option can be combined with Search Description.
  • Favorites shows only cards marked as favorites.
  • Favorite changes the selected card's saved favorite status.

Select a result to load its current artwork and enable its actions. A saved modded name appears in the editor context alongside the original name.

Use Ctrl-click to select multiple cards or Shift-click to select a range for mass editing.

docs.title: Replace card artwork
docs.text:
1. Select a card.
  2. Choose a PNG or JPEG with Select, or drag it onto the page.
  3. Check Preview.
  4. Choose Replace.

Use Stretch to fill the target texture or Crop to select a region with the target aspect ratio. Drag the crop to reposition it and use the mouse wheel to zoom. The preview is resized to the dimensions shown beside the image controls. Selecting another card resets the crop for its target dimensions. Current artwork, previews, and result thumbnails preserve their texture aspect ratios. Current and Preview images stay centered beneath their headings when the window size or card dimensions change.

docs.title: Overframe cards
docs.text:
Overframe cards use a 704 × 1024 replacement canvas, with portrait previews and a matching crop. Use PNG to preserve transparency outside the illustrated subject. The Overframe switch shows the selected card’s current framing. A tall texture alone does not identify an overframe card: Pendulum cards can also have tall textures.

Uncheck Overframe to switch the selected card to normal framing. This saves the framing change immediately and changes the replacement preview to 512 × 512. Select or crop a suitable normal illustration, then choose Replace. Changing framing does not generate a normal illustration or replace the texture automatically. Close the game while editing and restart it to check the result.

You can also enable Overframe for supported normal cards. Check it, prepare a transparent image in the portrait preview, and choose Replace. The switch changes framing immediately; it does not create new artwork. Normal Pendulum textures keep their existing dimensions until overframe is enabled.

Check Overframe again after disabling it to restore that card’s saved framing, then replace its artwork if needed. Other cards are unaffected. Image Restore restores only the artwork; use Overframe separately to change framing.

Original framing is backed up automatically under backups/cards/full_art for each player profile, even if image backups are disabled. Clearing these backups prevents the control from restoring the original framing exactly. Game updates and other mods can change framing; reselect the card to refresh its status.

If an update changes the gate bundle's location, Locate overframe data appears. Select the bundle containing the of_card_asset TextAsset from the game's LocalData/<account>/0000 or masterduel_Data/StreamingAssets/AssetBundle folders. The app validates the TextAsset before using it; this selection lasts for the current Cards tab session. When the gate is unavailable, framing changes are disabled and artwork editing uses the current texture's dimensions.

docs.title: Edit one card's text
docs.text:
Choose Edit Text to open the selected card's dialog.

  • Edit Name and Description, then choose Replace.
  • Restore Name and Restore Description put the original values back into the dialog before saving.
  • Both fields must remain non-empty for a direct replacement.

The same dialog can apply a Python regular-expression replacement to the selected card. Enter a pattern and replacement, choose Names and/or Descriptions, then use Apply Regex to Card. Capture groups such as \1 are supported in replacement text.

docs.title: Mass edit card text
docs.text:
Mass Edit applies a Python regular-expression replacement to All cards, Selected cards, Search results, or Favorites in the current TCG/OCG region. Each scope shows its card count. Choose whether to replace names, descriptions, or both; existing text edits are used as the starting text.

Click Preview Changes to see how many cards will change and the replacement count. Choose an affected card to compare its before/after text. In Differences, removed lines are red, added lines are green, headers are blue and bold, and newline notes are muted and italic. Colors adapt to light and dark themes; the - and + prefixes also identify removals and additions.

Choose Apply Changes after reviewing the preview. Changing the expression, replacement, fields, or scope requires another preview. Empty scopes and replacements that leave text unchanged cannot be applied.

See Regex mass editing for scope details and replacement syntax.

docs.title: Extract, copy, and restore
docs.text:
• Extract writes the card texture to images\cards.
  • Copy writes the complete bundle to bundles\cards.
  • Cards stored directly in data.unity3d can be extracted but cannot be copied as standalone bundles.
  • Restore writes the automatic image backup back to the selected card.

Card-text edits are tracked separately from image backups. Use Configuration's text Restore All or Reapply All for bulk text maintenance.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Card text changes can take significantly longer than image replacement. Wait for the completion message before closing the app.
  • Search uses the original card text, not a saved modded name or description.
  • Enable backups before the first artwork replacement if you want per-card Restore to work.

docs.title: Coin Editor
docs.text: The Coin Editor replaces duel coin textures and keeps the game's small, medium, and large versions together.

docs.title: Find an asset
docs.text:
Results show asset names. Hover over a shortened label to see its full name. The selected asset's name also appears above the editor. Assets without a translated name retain their code.

Type at least three characters in the search bar, then press Enter, click Search, or choose a completion suggestion. Search matches part of the name without case sensitivity. Clear the search bar to show all results again.

Favorites shows all favorites independently of the search; turning it off restores the last executed search.

After updating the app, use Check in Configuration to download the new names, then restart the app. Favorites and backups are preserved.

docs.title: Replace a coin
docs.text:
1. Select a coin from Results.
  2. Choose a square PNG or JPEG with Select, or drag it onto the page.
  3. Check Preview and choose Replace.

The app creates the required small, medium, and large square textures from the same source image. Use a square source to prevent distortion; PNG is recommended for transparency.

docs.title: Other actions
docs.text:
• Favorite marks the selected coin; Favorites filters the result grid.
  • Extract saves all three size textures under images\coins.
  • Copy saves all three Unity bundles under bundles\coins.
  • Restore uses the backup of the largest version to rebuild all three sizes.

Enable backups before the first replacement. Only the largest original texture is stored as the automatic backup.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: Configuration controls the game path, app data, automatic backups, card-text maintenance, appearance, and settings used when writing Unity bundles. Open it using the gear icon in the navigation toolbar.

docs.title: Game Path
docs.text:
The path must be the active player-ID folder under Master Duel's LocalData directory. Auto-detect searches the main Steam installation and configured Steam library folders. Select lets you browse manually.

After changing the path, restart the application so every editor loads data for that profile. See Getting started for an example path.

docs.title: Metadata Source
docs.text:
Use Metadata Source only if you need an alternative source for the app’s card and asset data. Enter the GitHub repository as owner/repository and, optionally, a Branch. Leave Branch blank to use the repository’s default. Choose Save source to save your selection, or Use defaults to return to Nauder/floowandereeze-and-modding-etl.

Choose Check to download data from the selected source. Changing the source refreshes the data even if its version date is older, while preserving your saved edits and backups. After updating, choose Refresh card list in Summons or restart the app to refresh the other editors. An alternative source must provide data compatible with the app.

docs.title: App Data Version
docs.text:
Choose Check to compare the installed data index with the current version and download updates when necessary. The update covers sleeves, cards, card icons, faces, wallpapers, fields, player icons, deck boxes, card metadata, coins, and available summon animations.

The update progress cannot be cancelled. Let all tasks finish, then restart the application if editor contents do not refresh immediately.

docs.title: Appearance
docs.text:
Choose or drag an image to use as the application's background. This changes only the modding tool, not Master Duel.

  • Stretched fills the window and may distort the image.
  • Cropped preserves the aspect ratio and crops overflow.
  • Reset removes the custom image.

Changes are applied immediately. A darker image usually keeps labels and controls easier to read.

docs.title: Card Text
docs.text:
• Reapply All writes every saved modded card name and description back to the current game metadata. This is useful after a game update.
  • Restore All writes the original names and descriptions back for every card with saved edits.

Both actions can take a long time. Confirm the prompt and leave the application open until it reports completion. Restoring text in the game does not erase the saved modded values, so they can be reapplied later.

docs.title: Backups
docs.text:
• Enable Backups before replacing assets to save the original texture on the first replacement.
  • Restore All restores every asset for which the app has a backup.
  • Clear Backups permanently deletes every automatic backup.

Bulk restore and clear operations ask for confirmation. Backups consume local disk space and are stored beside the application under backups.

docs.title: Packer
docs.text: The packer controls compression when the app saves modified Unity bundles. Available choices are None, LZMA, LZ4, LZ4HC, and LZHAM. LZ4 is the default and is the safest choice unless you have a specific compatibility or size requirement.

docs.title: Mipmap Count
docs.text:
This controls the number of mipmap levels generated for supported replacement textures. The default is 10. Lower values may reduce file size but can make distant or downscaled textures look worse; unusually high values may not suit small images.

These settings affect replacements made after the setting changes. Some special assets use fixed texture settings and do not use the global mipmap count.

docs.title: Safety notes
docs.text:
Use the Backups tab to view, selectively remove, export, or import saved backups by category, all files, or manual selection. Clear Backups removes the same inventory, including nested overframe backups.

  • Backups are not retroactive.
  • Game updates and other mods can overwrite changed bundles.
  • Clear Backups cannot be undone from within the app.
  • Selecting another player profile changes which game files the app modifies, but the app's saved preferences and edits remain in its local database.

Choose Check to update accessory names, then restart the app to refresh labels and search suggestions. See Sleeves, Player Icons, Card Icons, Coins, and Deck Boxes for search instructions.

docs.title: Summon animation data
docs.text: Choose Check to download available summon animation data. Some data sources may not include summon animations; other editors will still work. The Summon Animation Editor uses your configured game version and game path automatically.

docs.title: Deck Box Editor
docs.text: The Deck Box Editor replaces deck box artwork and handles its different resolutions automatically.

docs.title: Find an asset
docs.text:
Results show asset names. Hover over a shortened label to see its full name. The selected asset's name also appears above the editor. Assets without a translated name retain their code.

Type at least three characters in the search bar, then press Enter, click Search, or choose a completion suggestion. Search matches part of the name without case sensitivity. Clear the search bar to show all results again.

Favorites shows all favorites independently of the search; turning it off restores the last executed search.

After updating the app, use Check in Configuration to download the new names, then restart the app. Favorites and backups are preserved.

docs.title: Replace a deck box
docs.text:
1. Open Deck Boxes and select a box from Results.
  2. Choose its Texture variant: Normal, Left Facing, or Open.
  3. Use Select or drop a PNG or JPEG onto the page.
  4. Choose Stretch or Crop and check Preview.
  5. Choose Replace, then check the result in Master Duel.

Current and Preview use the large version of the selected orientation. Replace applies the same artwork to all matching resolutions automatically, preserving each texture's dimensions. Normal includes small, medium, and large; Left Facing and Open each include medium and large. Other orientations remain unchanged. Replacement artwork can fill the whole image without being clipped to the original box silhouette. PNG transparency still controls the visible shape. Reapply Replace to fix a deck box edited with an older version of the app.

docs.title: Other actions
docs.text:
• Favorite marks the deck box; Favorites filters Results.
  • Extract saves the large texture of the selected orientation under images\deck_boxes.
  • Copy saves all Unity bundles for the selected orientation under bundles\deck_boxes.
  • Restore restores all resolutions of the selected orientation from backups\deck_boxes.

Enable backups in Configuration before replacing textures. Each resolution gets its own backup before its first replacement; existing backups are preserved. Restore requires backups for all resolutions of the selected orientation, and restores each original texture separately. Older backups made for only one resolution can still be restored individually through Configuration's bulk restore. Configuration's bulk restore and clear actions also include deck box backups.

Restore puts back the original artwork and transparency, but keeps the full rectangular image area used by replacements. If game files are missing, complete the in-game download before editing. Use Check in Configuration to refresh outdated asset data.

docs.title: Card Face Editor
docs.text: The Card Face Editor changes the frame/face textures that surround card artwork.

docs.title: Replace a face
docs.text:
1. Select a face from the list.
  2. Choose a portrait PNG or JPEG with Select, or drag it onto the page.
  3. Compare Current and Preview.
  4. Choose Replace.

Use the extracted original as a template when alignment and transparent regions matter.

docs.title: Extract and restore
docs.text:
• Extract saves the selected texture under images\faces with a filesystem-safe version of its name.
  • Restore writes the automatic backup back to the selected face.

Enable backups before the first replacement if you want Restore to work.

docs.title: Important limitation
docs.text: Card faces are stored inside masterduel_Data\data.unity3d. A game update or another mod that replaces that file can remove face changes and other edits stored in the same file.

docs.title: Duel Field Editor
docs.text: The Duel Field Editor replaces the supported playable surface region of a duel field.

docs.title: Replace a field
docs.text:
1. Select a field from Results.
  2. Choose a PNG or JPEG with Select, or drag it onto the page.
  3. Check Preview and choose Replace.
  4. Test the result in a duel from both player perspectives.

docs.title: Extract and copy
docs.text:
• Extract saves the supported field texture under images\fields.
  • Copy saves the complete Unity bundle under bundles\fields.

This editor does not currently provide per-field backup or Restore controls. Make an extracted texture and bundle copy before replacing a field.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text: Master Duel fields are not standardized. Fields whose texture layout is not recognized are omitted from the list. Some listed fields may still replace the wrong region or appear flipped. Check the result in-game before keeping a replacement.

docs.title: Player Icon Editor
docs.text: The Player Icon Editor replaces profile icons and manages the small, medium, and large bundles as one asset.

docs.title: Find an asset
docs.text:
Results show asset names. Hover over a shortened label to see its full name. The selected asset's name also appears above the editor. Assets without a translated name retain their code.

Type at least three characters in the search bar, then press Enter, click Search, or choose a completion suggestion. Search matches part of the name without case sensitivity. Clear the search bar to show all results again.

Favorites shows all favorites independently of the search; turning it off restores the last executed search.

After updating the app, use Check in Configuration to download the new names, then restart the app. Favorites and backups are preserved.

docs.title: Replace an icon
docs.text:
1. Select an icon from Results.
  2. Choose a square PNG or JPEG with Select, or drag it onto the page.
  3. Check Preview and choose Replace.

The app resizes the source and writes all three icon resolutions. Use a square image to avoid distortion; PNG is recommended when transparency matters. Current displays the medium version.

docs.title: Other actions
docs.text:
• Favorite marks the selected icon; Favorites filters the result grid.
  • Extract saves all three textures under images\icons.
  • Copy saves all three Unity bundles under bundles\icons.
  • Restore uses the backup of the largest version to rebuild all three sizes.

Enable backups before the first replacement. Only the largest original texture is stored as the automatic backup.

docs.title: Card Sleeve Editor
docs.text: The Card Sleeve Editor replaces sleeve textures and can add an optional colored border.

docs.title: Find an asset
docs.text:
Results show asset names. Hover over a shortened label to see its full name. The selected asset's name also appears above the editor. Assets without a translated name retain their code.

Type at least three characters in the search bar, then press Enter, click Search, or choose a completion suggestion. Search matches part of the name without case sensitivity. Clear the search bar to show all results again.

Favorites shows all favorites independently of the search; turning it off restores the last executed search.

After updating the app, use Check in Configuration to download the new names, then restart the app. Favorites and backups are preserved.

docs.title: Replace a sleeve
docs.text:
1. Select a sleeve from Results.
  2. Choose a portrait PNG or JPEG with Select, or drag it onto the page.
  3. Optionally configure the border.
  4. Choose Replace.

Match the portrait aspect ratio shown by the current sleeve to avoid stretching.

docs.title: Add a border
docs.text:
1. Choose the border color with the color Select button.
  2. Enable Use Border.
  3. Optionally enable Fade-in Effect for a softer transition into the artwork.

The preview shows the border color but does not fully render the fade. The complete effect is generated during replacement. Disabling Use Border also disables the fade.

docs.title: Other actions
docs.text:
• Favorite marks the selected sleeve; Favorites filters the results.
  • Extract saves the texture under images\sleeves.
  • Copy saves the complete Unity bundle under bundles\sleeves.
  • Restore writes the automatic backup back to the selected sleeve.

Enable backups before the first replacement if you want Restore to work.

docs.title: Summon Animation Editor
docs.text:
The Summons tab uses the animation icon in the navigation toolbar.

The Summons tab replaces a monster's summon animation from a GIF, MP4 video or individual PNG frames. Select the card and your input; the app chooses the matching animation assets automatically.

docs.title: Replace an animation
docs.text:
1. In Configuration, set your Game Path and choose TCG for the Global game or OCG for the OCG game. Summons uses these settings automatically, including any additional installed game assets.
  2. Open Summons and search for the card by name or ID.
  3. Leave Replace the lower-quality animation instead unchecked to replace high quality. Check it to replace lower quality instead. The other version keeps its artwork unless the card shares the same skeleton between quality modes; the preview and confirmation warn when both modes will change.
  4. Choose Choose GIF / MP4 or PNG folder, or drop one local GIF/MP4 file or a folder containing PNG frames anywhere in the Summons tab. The preview prepares automatically in the right-hand panel. MP4 frame timing is retained; audio is ignored.
  5. Play or scrub the inline preview. Open Adjust timing, size and position only if you want to change the defaults, then press Update preview.
  6. Close Master Duel and press Replace animation. Original files are backed up automatically.

Large inputs show a Large animation import memory estimate before frame conversion. Choose Yes to continue or No to cancel. This warning can be overridden; incompatible formats, playback structures and atlas capacity still prevent replacement. See memory estimates and limits.

Drag the divider to resize the card list. Input, playback, settings and replacement controls stay in the tab; expanded controls scroll on smaller windows.

The source stays selected when you change cards or quality, and the preview rebuilds for the new target. A drop before card selection is retained until you select a card. Empty folders, single PNG files, remote URLs and multiple dropped items are ignored. Decoding errors appear in the preview panel. Target controls and additional drops are disabled while the app prepares or replaces an animation.

See the GIF, MP4 and PNG guide for input formats, timing and limits.

Summons uses your current Configuration settings when reopened. Choose Refresh card list after updating app data. It only uses assets from your selected game version and installation.

If the selected quality is unavailable, choose the other quality using the checkbox. Missing game downloads or outdated app data can also prevent replacement. Complete the in-game download and choose Check in Configuration before trying again. See compatibility details for cards with additional effects.

docs.title: Back up and restore
docs.text:
Original animation files are always backed up under backups/summon_animations, even when image backups are disabled. Later replacements keep the first backup.

Select the card and press Restore original animation. The app chooses all verified backups for that card automatically, including both quality versions and shared playback data. Confirmation identifies other cards when they share affected files. Restoration replaces complete bundles, so it also reverts edits sharing those files.

Use the Backups tab to export/import the Summon Animations category. Keep each manifest.json and its adjacent original.bundle together. ZIP import changes backups only. Automatic remapping to a different local installation remains unsupported.

docs.title: Summon compatibility audit
docs.text:
This developer command checks every summon card available in the configured metadata against the real replacement pipeline. It uses the same Global/OCG installation, game path and preferred regional assets as the Summons tab.

From the repository root, run:

.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe tools/audit_summon_animations.py

Reports are saved to build/summon-audit/report.json and report.csv. JSON includes per-card, per-quality, per-format results and the failure stage. CSV provides a flat list for filtering. If a spreadsheet locks the CSV file, JSON progress continues; close the CSV to allow its next refresh.

Progress logs use UTF-8 so card names such as Evil★Twin can be printed safely on Windows. Watch a redirected log with Get-Content -Encoding UTF8 -Tail 10 -Wait path/to/audit.log.

The full audit can take hours for a large collection: texture compression runs for every supported card. Results update after each card. Each card runs in an isolated process, with two processes by default, and a 180-second timeout. A timeout or native crash is recorded as a failure and the remaining cards continue.

docs.title: What is checked
docs.text:
• Every card with skeleton metadata, including alternate artworks.
  • Every available high/lower quality target, using synthetic GIF and PNG inputs.
  • Actual timeline references, dependencies, profiles, materials and supported prefab components.
  • Framing, atlas capacity and frame generation at the GUI defaults: 256-pixel long edge and 30 output FPS.
  • Texture encoding, compressed format/mipmap preservation, bundle save/reload, and unchanged objects/resources.

The synthetic input has two different frames, transparent padding and opaque artwork. When GIF and PNG produce exactly the same pixels, timing, target metadata and dependency checksums, native serialization is performed once for that quality; the other format records which result it reuses.

The service discards generated bundle bytes after validation. It creates no game backups, changes no game files and does not update the application's database. Reports must be outside the game asset and backup directories and must not overwrite the database. Only reports and temporary synthetic input are written.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
# Faster generation/validation scan; skips texture encoding and save/reload
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe tools/audit_summon_animations.py --preview-only --report build/summon-audit/preview.json

# Check selected cards
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe tools/audit_summon_animations.py --card 20567 --card 20569

# Resume an interrupted run with unchanged metadata, settings, importer code and dependency bytes
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe tools/audit_summon_animations.py --resume

# Try smaller frames when investigating atlas capacity failures
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe tools/audit_summon_animations.py --edge 32 --report build/summon-audit/small-frames.json

Use --jobs 1 through --jobs 4 to control parallelism, --timeout to change the per-card limit, and --database to use another local database snapshot. To rerun previously failed cards after changing the importer, start a fresh report rather than resuming results from the previous implementation. Resume reuses only passed cards whose dependency checksums still match; failures and missing assets are retried.

docs.title: Fixing failures in batches
docs.text:
Use the JSON/CSV failure list to group cards by their error, then rerun just that group with a separate report after a fix:

.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe tools/audit_summon_animations.py --card 12590 --card 16386 --report build/summon-audit/batch-1.json

Keep the batch report separate from the catalog scan so progress is not overwritten. Each worker records the importer revision it tested. A scan freezes its importer modules in a temporary snapshot, so edits made for another batch do not invalidate workers that are already queued. Resume still requires unchanged importer code; start a new report after fixes to test the new revision. Rerun affected cards against the final revision before claiming catalog compatibility.

docs.title: Reading results
docs.text:
Status Meaning passed Every available quality and input format passed the selected audit mode. failed At least one compatibility, generation, encoding, verification or worker check failed. Read its stage and error. missing_assets Required mapped bundles are not downloaded; compatibility could not be checked.

A graph failure applies to both formats and all quality modes because they share the same playback validation. Other failures remain specific to their input format and quality. Cards without skeleton metadata do not appear in the audit because they are not selectable summon replacements.

An incomplete JSON report has complete: false. Do not treat its current counts as the final catalog result. Exit code 0 means the entire selected catalog passed; code 1 means there were failures or missing assets.

Passing checks means this synthetic input completed the requested pipeline. It does not guarantee that arbitrary GIFs/PNG sequences fit the atlas, or that the replacement looks correct in-game. Use the GIF/PNG guide for limits and verify playback, placement and shaders in the game.

Synthetic regression coverage runs without installed game assets:

.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m unittest discover -s tests -p test_summon_audit.py

docs.title: GIF, MP4 and PNG summon animations
docs.text:
Choose a card in Summons, then press Choose GIF / MP4 or PNG folder, or drop a GIF/MP4 file or PNG frames folder into the tab. The editor finds the correct animation automatically using the game version and path from Configuration.

High quality is selected by default. Check Replace the lower-quality animation instead before choosing your input to target lower quality. The other quality keeps its artwork, including any earlier replacement, unless both modes use the same skeleton. Shared-quality cards show a warning in the preview and replacement confirmation.

docs.title: Preview and replace
docs.text:
The preview prepares automatically in the same tab after choosing or dropping the input. It stays selected when you switch cards or quality, and the preview rebuilds for the new target. Play/pause or scrub it, then close Master Duel and press Replace animation.

PNG files sort naturally: frame1.png, frame2.png, frame10.png. Non-PNG files in the folder are ignored. GIF frames use their individual delays, disposal and transparency. GIF loop counts do not extend the summon clip.

MP4 imports use the first video stream and its frame timestamps, including variable frame rates. Audio is ignored. Ordinary MP4 video has an opaque background; use GIF or PNG frames for transparent artwork. The PNG source FPS setting affects PNG sequences only. Video uses the same fit/crop, output FPS, timing, preview and replacement controls as GIFs.

MP4 support is included in the packaged app; no additional video tools are required.

Defaults fit the source to the original summon duration at 30 FPS, with a 256-pixel long edge and transparent padding.

Open Adjust timing, size and position for optional controls:

Control Behavior PNG source FPS Playback speed of an image sequence. Output FPS Number of sampled output frames per second. Frame resolution Long edge of each frame; lower it if capacity is exceeded. Fit / Crop Add transparent padding or crop to fill the original framing bounds. Size and offsets Scale and position the artwork; positive vertical offsets move upward. Fit timing Stretch/compress the source to the original summon duration. Keep speed Trim long input; hold the last frame of short input.

Changing settings clears the preview and disables replacement until you choose Update preview. The preview displays generated frames and framing, rather than the full game camera, effects, audio or shader behavior.

docs.title: Limits
docs.text:
• GIF, MP4 video and individual PNG frames are supported. Animated PNG and other video file extensions are unsupported. Corrupt files, unsupported codecs and MP4s without usable video or timing show an import error.
  • Large inputs, or videos whose memory use cannot be estimated, show Large animation import before conversion. Choose Yes to continue or No to cancel. The estimate is approximate; actual memory use can be higher.
  • Cancelling clears the preview and disables replacement. Shorten or downscale the source, or lower Frame resolution, to reduce memory use. Lowering Output FPS alone may not reduce the memory needed to read the source.
  • The memory warning can appear again when you change the source, settings, card or quality, or update the preview.
  • Output supports 1–60 FPS, a 32–1024-pixel long edge and a clip no longer than ten seconds.
  • The selected card’s animation files have limited space for frames. If the animation does not fit, lower Frame resolution, lower Output FPS, or shorten the clip.
  • Some cards have unsupported animation structures or effects. The app reports a compatibility error and prevents replacement. Refresh app data and complete the game’s asset download if the error indicates missing or outdated files.

Select the card and choose Restore original animation to restore both quality versions to their backed-up state. See backup and restore details.

docs.title: Shared playback compatibility
docs.text:
Some cards, including Fiendsmith Engraver in Global assets, share an animation between high and low quality. Replacing either quality can affect both. Review the shared-quality warning in the preview and replacement confirmation before proceeding.

For cards with separate quality versions, the unselected version keeps its existing artwork, including earlier replacements. Restoring the original animation restores both versions.

docs.title: Custom materials and effect tracks
docs.text:
Cards such as Fallen of Albaz, Aluber the Jester of Despia and Archfiend Emperor have additional visual effects. Supported effects are preserved, but the preview does not show all game effects, lighting or camera behavior. Some effects may also affect how your replacement looks.

Always check placement, transparency and playback in-game at the quality you replaced before sharing a mod. Compatibility checks cannot guarantee the final appearance. If a card’s effects or playback are unsupported, the app prevents replacement; try another card or restore its original animation.

docs.title: Wallpaper Editor
docs.text:
The Wallpaper Editor changes home-screen wallpaper assets, which use separate foreground and background bundles.

The scrollable wallpaper selector stays 240 logical pixels wide on the left, with complete thumbnails. The selected artwork uses the remaining width without squeezing the list, including when the window is maximized.

docs.title: Replace a wallpaper
docs.text:
1. Select a wallpaper from the list.
  2. Choose a PNG or JPEG with Select, or drag it onto the page.
  3. Choose Replace.

The source is scaled down to fit the existing foreground canvas without changing its aspect ratio, placed at the canvas origin, and written over transparency. The background layer is replaced with a transparent image.

For predictable placement, prepare the source at the same dimensions shown for the selected foreground and put any intended transparent padding into the source image itself.

docs.title: Extract, copy, and restore
docs.text:
• Extract saves both foreground and background textures under images\wallpapers.
  • Copy saves both Unity bundles under bundles\wallpapers.
  • Restore rebuilds the wallpaper using the backed-up foreground image and the editor's normal transparent-background behavior.

Enable backups before the first replacement if you want Restore to work.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text: Some wallpapers contain more than two visual layers or separate effects such as sparks. The editor changes the main foreground, removes the designated background layer, and leaves extra layers and effects untouched. Those untouched elements may remain visible over a replacement.
